weeklySignals.title: Figma agent
weeklySignals.summary: Generally available since 6 October, with library guidelines, file search, and custom skills. It now uses AI credits. Test one library-backed edit and inspect the result before adopting it.

weeklySignals.title: Figma Motion
weeklySignals.summary: The 30 September update adds reusable animation styles and Lottie export. Try one component animation to check the handoff; Motion remains in open beta.

weeklySignals.title: Framer Skills
weeklySignals.summary: Released 22 September, newly reviewed for our collection: reusable instructions for design systems, copy, and CMS work. Test whether one skill keeps a second page consistent.

tools.title: Figma MCP
tools.description: Figma’s official MCP reads design context and can create or update native frames, components, variables, and auto layout through supported clients and Figma skills.
tools.recommendation: Use it to connect design context with implementation and editable canvas work. The remote server has the broadest feature set; verify generated changes against the actual components and layout.

tools.title: Playwright MCP
tools.description: Lets an AI agent inspect and operate browser interfaces through structured accessibility data for repeatable product checks and walkthroughs.
tools.recommendation: A dependable bridge between product intent and browser evidence. Make automated actions observable and keep sensitive sessions out of tests.

tools.title: Apple Design Skill
tools.description: A reusable skill for checking Apple-platform interface work against platform design guidance and implementation conventions.
tools.recommendation: Useful as a platform-specific review lens. Treat its output as critique support and confirm important decisions against current Apple guidance.

tools.title: Emil Kowalski’s skills
tools.description: A compact collection of design-engineering skills focused on motion, interface detail, and more intentional frontend execution.
tools.recommendation: Strong material for raising the quality bar in implementation. Best used selectively, with the team’s own interaction principles layered on top.

tools.title: Scroll Craft
tools.description: A skill for planning and refining scroll-driven experiences, including pacing, transitions, and implementation choices.
tools.recommendation: A focused prompt layer for a difficult interaction pattern. Test for reduced motion, input diversity, and performance before treating a result as finished.

tools.title: Mobbin MCP
tools.description: Connects AI workflows to Mobbin’s library of real product screens and flows for faster pattern research and comparison.
tools.recommendation: Helpful for grounding early exploration in shipped products. Use references to understand patterns, not to converge on copied solutions.

tools.title: Savee MCP
tools.description: Searches Savee’s curated reference library and can retrieve personal saves, boards, and feed items inside supported AI clients.
tools.recommendation: Promising for bringing a team’s visual references closer to ideation. Keep generated output distinct from the source material and retain links to references.

tools.title: ScreensDesign MCP
tools.description: Provides read-only access to real mobile screens, full recordings, paywalls, onboarding, and user flows from a large app library.
tools.recommendation: A useful research layer for flow-level comparison, especially when isolated screenshots hide interaction context. Validate coverage for your market before relying on it.

tools.title: Cosmos
tools.description: A visual discovery and collecting tool for organizing references, exploring related imagery, and building a durable taste library.
tools.recommendation: Useful now because it supports the slow work of collecting and organizing taste, not only generating output. Shared clusters can also make critique references more concrete.

tools.title: Ploy
tools.description: An AI website builder for drafting marketing pages from an existing site and brand system, with reusable sections and components.
tools.recommendation: Interesting for constrained page drafting because it starts from existing brand material. We still need to test how well it preserves hierarchy and system logic at scale.

tools.title: Raylight
tools.description: A motion-design editor for turning product interfaces into polished launch and product videos with AI-assisted canvas edits.
tools.recommendation: Try it on a single product shot or hero video before moving larger motion narratives into production.

tools.title: Geometric
tools.description: A browser-based image and motion art tool for transforming source material through configurable geometric and visual effects.
tools.recommendation: Useful as a deliberate visual detour when a team needs material beyond interface references. Its value is exploration, not automatic brand fit.

tools.title: Canva MCP
tools.description: Canva’s official remote MCP supports design generation and editing, design-library search, brand and asset management, export, and collaborative comments.
tools.recommendation: Use it when you need AI-assisted design creation or edits inside Canva, and check permissions plus brand fidelity on one small workflow first.

tools.title: Canva Skills
tools.description: Canva’s official skills package adds reusable creative workflows on top of the Canva Connector for Codex, Claude, and Cursor.
tools.recommendation: A credible official workflow layer rather than an unverified prompt pack. Review the active skill subset and keep Canva authentication scoped to the intended team account.

tools.title: Pinterest MCP
tools.description: Pinterest’s announced official MCP is intended to search Pins, explore and manage Boards, follow trends, and surface audience and advertising insights.
tools.recommendation: The official page shows an endpoint and scoped authorization but still invites launch sign-ups. Keep watching until access and personal-board permissions are confirmed in a working account.

tools.title: UI Design Agent Kit
tools.description: A project-level UI agent workflow that turns plain-language briefs into a design contract, implementation plan, browser checks, and recorded delivery evidence.
tools.recommendation: Its explicit design contract and browser evidence are promising. The kit is broad and opinionated, so test one bounded workflow before adopting its full tool routing.

tools.title: Seenry Skills
tools.description: An eight-skill design collection for research, composition, assets, motion, mobile UI, branding, decks, and video. Optional Seenry MCP adds captured-screen evidence.
tools.recommendation: Start with one skill, such as reference research or review, before adopting the full workflow.

tools.title: Dembrandt
tools.description: An MCP and CLI that extracts design tokens, typography, spacing, components, and accessibility findings from live websites.
tools.recommendation: Run it against a few reference sites to compare tokens and accessibility findings before using them as evidence.

tools.title: Diagram Design
tools.description: A Codex-compatible design skill for producing structured, editable diagrams, including user journeys and flow diagrams.
tools.recommendation: Apply it to one user journey or service flow, then compare the structure and labels against your current documentation.

tools.title: Figma Motion
tools.description: A timeline inside Figma Design for editable keyframe animation, reusable motion styles, and supported Lottie exports. The 30 September release extends its open beta.
tools.recommendation: Test one component animation and its exported result before moving a motion system. Reusable styles could reduce repeated setup; beta behavior and export fidelity still need a team trial.

tools.title: Framer Skills
tools.description: Project-level instructions for the Framer agent covering design systems, writing style, and CMS workflows. Skills can reference project pages, components, and styles and travel with a remix.
tools.recommendation: Capture one agreed design or content rule, then check whether the agent applies it consistently to a second page. Source-reviewed; the team still needs to test how reliably those rules hold.

tools.title: Iconiq UI
tools.description: An open-source UI collection delivered as editable local components through the shadcn registry, with an optional connection through shadcn MCP.
tools.recommendation: A team-submitted lead for restrained component motion. Check keyboard behavior, reduced motion, and design-system fit in a small prototype before recommending it for product work.

tools.title: Figma agent
tools.description: An agent inside Figma Design for generating and editing layouts, applying connected libraries, and getting design feedback.
tools.access: All plans; AI credits; editing depends on seat and file access
tools.setup: Open Agents in a Figma Design file
tools.recommendation: Try one bounded layout edit with a connected library, then verify component use, hierarchy, and access scope.

tools.title: Scenario Agent Skills
tools.description: A set of agent skills for producing images, video, audio, textures, skyboxes, and 3D assets through the Scenario MCP, with separate expert tools for Blender, Maya, ZBrush, Unreal, and Unity.
tools.recommendation: Source-reviewed; not yet team-tested. Use it for one small branded asset task, such as a single image or 3D concept, before expanding to a wider production workflow.
tools.setup: Not stated; check whether the MCP or local DCC tool path fits your workflow
